candidates.title: BLET, CPKC reach tentative agreement on new contract for Dakota, Minnesota & Eastern workers
candidates.excerpt: INDEPENDENCE, Ohio — The Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen has reached a tentative five-year agreement with CPKC covering workers on the railroad’s Dakota, Minnesota & Eastern territory. If ratified, the agreement would create parity between workers on the DM&E and those on the railroad’s former Soo Line territory by 2029, the union said. Over the life of the agreement, the hourly rate for engineers would increase by 41.42%, compounded, while conductors and brakemen would see increases of 32.63%, compounded. “This wage progression is one of the most significant components of the tentative agreement,” BLET General Chairman Nick Mugavero said in a press release. The agreement would be retroactive to Jan. 1, 2025. It also includes quality-of-life and work-rule enhancements such as an increased meal allowance and personal leave day flexibility. candidates.title: Rapido HO scale drop-bottom gondola review
candidates.excerpt: A Pressed Steel Car Co. drop-bottom gondola has been added to the Rapido Trains HO scale freight car lineup. The newly-tooled model, based on original CAD files designed by the Northern Pacific Railway Historical Association (NPRHA), features plastic and die-cast metal construction, 33″ metal wheelsets, and semi-scale metal couplers. The Rapido Trains model is based on Northern Pacific’s 50000 through 50499 series of drop-bottom gondolas built by Pressed Steel Car Co. Inc. in Pittsburgh, Pa., in 1940. The 500 cars were assigned to general service, hauling coal, ore, pulpwood, scrap metal, and sugar beets, among other commodities. From 1966 to 1968, some — but not all — of the cars from this series were reconditioned. As part of that process, the rehabbed gondolas were reassigned to the 58250 through 58749 series. candidates.title: IEA could consider more oil reserve releases as Europe faces tough winter
candidates.excerpt: IEA could consider more oil reserve releases as Europe faces tough winter The IEA says it could consider releasing more emergency oil stocks if supply disruptions worsen, although another release is not currently its top priority. Europe faces a difficult winter after spending more than €100bn extra on energy imports since the Iran war began. The IEA has hinted that releasing further strategic oil reserves could be an option to ease supply shortages. Speaking at a meeting of EU energy ministers in Dublin, International Energy Agency Executive Director Fatih Birol said that the agency has released 400 million barrels of crude oil from its strategic reserves since March and that one-third of that has yet to “come to the markets”. The released stocks are equivalent to “20% of the overall stocks”, Birol said, adding that “80% is still in our pocket. If there is a need and if our member countries do agree with it, we are ready to act in order to address current and future market challenges_

Seven of the 10 specific carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025. They were led by metallic ores and metals, 9.5%; petroleum and related products, 9.4%; and chemicals, 7.2%. candidates.title: U.S. weekly rail volume again above 2025 levels
candidates.excerpt: WASHINGTON — Continued intermodal strength again assured that weekly U.S. rail traffic remained above 2025 levels. The Association of American Railroads reports that traffic for the week ending Sept. 26, 2026, was 537,397 carloads and intermodal units, a gain of 4.8% compared to the same week a year ago. The overall figure included 235,787 carloads, up 3%, and 301,610 containers and trailers, up 6.3%. For the year to date, total volume is 19,458,578 carloads and intermodal units, an increase of 3.5% over the first 38 weeks of 2025. The 8,679,882 carloads represent a 2.7% increase while the 10,778,696 intermodal units are an increase of 4.1%. North American volume for the week, as reported by nine U.S., Canadian, and Mexican railroads, was 733,610 carloads and intermodal units, up 3.5% over the corresponding week a year ago. candidates.excerpt: The Surface Transportation Board has appointed Marty Schlenker as director of its Office of Economics and Terrence McDermott as senior adviser to Chairman Patrick Fuchs, adding two officials to the agency as it handles major rail competition, rate and merger matters. Fuchs announced the appointments Sept. 24, saying Schlenker’s selection was made with the Board’s approval. Both Schlenker and McDermott had been serving at the agency in temporary transition roles before receiving the permanent appointments. The appointments come as the STB’s workload includes its review of Union Pacific’s (NYSE: UNP) proposed acquisition of Norfolk Southern (NYSE: NSC). The 25 crew of the vessel were reported to have abandoned ship into a lifeboat and were rescued by another MSC vessel MSC Ruby which answered the distress call. Two other MSC vessels MSC Florentina and the MSC Turin III also diverted to the vicinity of the MSC Hermes III that appeared to be adrift around 300 km east of Vietnam. candidates.excerpt: A BNSF train carrying mixed freight caught fire during a burglary in Riverside, California, Thursday morning. The train was traveling from Los Angeles to Chicago, BNSF told FreightWaves. Firefighters found an open upper container burning on the moving double-stack train. Officials have not identified the items inside or reported any stolen cargo. Riverside dispatchers received the first report at 4:40 a.m. near Chicago Avenue. Early information placed the train heading west from downtown. Crews later located it moving east between Spruce and Columbia streets. Riverside Fire Department deployed 19 firefighters, four engines, one truck and a chief officer. Crews move train for access Access problems prevented crews from reaching the flames at their first location. Incident commanders directed railroad personnel to reposition the equipment farther east.
